summary: Working in Buddhist and computational studies, Richard B. Mahoney earned his MA from the University of Canterbury by 2002 under supervisor Paul Harrison, where he also held a post attested in 2001.
Richard B. Martin worked in Tibetology and Indology. He held posts at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983-1991) and as a South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker, working in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Shunryu Suzuki and at Harvard, UC Berkeley, Wisconsin-Madison, Minnesota, and Colorado Boulder. He led the San Francisco Zen Center (1971-1984) and held posts at the University of Iowa (1970-1999).
Richard Barron is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Richard Bertram Whitehead (1879-1967) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Liverpool College, Exeter College, Oxford, and the University of Cambridge (D.Litt. by 1940), serving as Fellow-Commoner and Advisor to Indian students at St John's College in 1922.

Richard Bowring, a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, earned his degrees at the University of Cambridge. He taught at Columbia and Princeton before becoming Master of Selwyn College (2000-2012) and Emeritus Professor at Cambridge.

Richard Burghart (1944-1994) worked in Indology and religious studies, completing degrees at Williams College and SOAS University of London. He taught Asian anthropology at SOAS (~1979-1988) and London School of Economics, later becoming Professor of Anthropology at Heidelberg University in 1988.
Richard Burn (1871-1947), active in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Christ Church, Oxford (~1889-1893). He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1893 to 1927.

Richard Carnac Temple (1850-1931) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, he served in the Bengal Staff Corps (~1877-1891), the Indian Staff Corps (~1891-1904), and edited the Indian Antiquary (~1885-1931).

Richard Constant Boer (1863-1929) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Groningen, where he was a Privatdozent (1888-1900), and served as Professor of Old Germanic and Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam (1900-1929).

Richard D. Mann specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University under doctoral supervisor Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2007).

Richard D. McBride II specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Mentored by Robert E. Buswell Jr., he received his PhD from UCLA in 2001 and served as Associate Professor of Asian and Near Eastern Languages at Brigham Young University (attested 2019).

Richard De Smet (1916-1997) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Robert Antoine and Michel Ledrus, earned a Ph.D. from the Pontifical Gregorian University, and became Professor of Logic, Metaphysics and Indian Philosophy at De Nobili College in 1954.

Archaeologist Richard Delbrück (1875-1957) studied at Neuchâtel, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn (Ph.D.). He directed the German Archaeological Institute at Rome (1911-1915) and held professorships at Jena (~1911-1928), Giessen (1922-1928), and Bonn (1928-1940).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who earned his AM and PhD at the University of Chicago. He was Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University Bloomington (2013-2021).

Richard Fick (1867-1944) studied Indology at Kiel University (Ph.D.) under Richard Pischel and Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at the Prussian State Library, became director of the Göttingen State and University Library (1921-1932), and was an honorary professor at Göttingen.

id: P:Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John
summary: Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John (1839-1919) studied at Wadham College and worked in linguistics and Indology. He taught Hindûstânî and Burmese at the University of Oxford between ~1884 and 1910, and Burmese at University College London in 1894.

Richard Foltz works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and history. He studied at the University of Utah and Harvard University, taught at the University of Florida (2000-2005), and served as Founding Director of the Centre for Iranian Studies at Concordia University.
Richard Francis Burton (1821-1890) worked in Indology, religious studies, and other fields. He studied at Trinity College, Oxford in 1840.

Richard Fritzsche (1851-) studied Indology at the University of Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and Georg Curtius. He taught at Königliches Gymnasium Chemnitz (1876-1888) and served as Rektor of Gymnasium Schneeberg (~1899-1916).
